top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a concrete, mature discovery with a clear originator (Katori's magic-wavelength lattice) and a clear second contributor (Ye, taking it to 10^-18 and into many-body regimes). The 10^-18 claim is verified by independent laboratory comparisons, and the clocks now yield results about nature (redshift tests over millimetres, constancy of constants, many-body spin physics). The two-name allocation is clean and the citation scope is well supported, so I prefer awarding it to no award.
